name: 1615–1617 Indiana Avenue — Brick dwelling (district draft; refined by T-1946)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): 'Two 3B brick dwellings (D), 1615 and 1617, behind a stone (blue) strip along their Indiana front, small one-storey frame pieces at their rear'. Carried to 1904 on the T-3019 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3019, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1946 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 20w trace (s20wfp-indiana_1615-b1), the T-3019 census (s20w-1615-front) and the T-1837 register row frontage-20w-1615–1617 (Brick dwelling); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-background-3019).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-3019 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1615 S. Indiana Avenue, parcel indiana_1615 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Indiana Avenue, the background behind Prairie Avenue: Indiana Avenue's east frontage, 16th to 18th Street, and East Sixteenth Street's row at 209-217 (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20, checked lot by lot against Robinson 1886 plate 10).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 26.750, v -0.305 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.445 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front), widened to 5.5 m along the front because the fitted strip was narrower than any house of the avenue (T-2690). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '3B; rear3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 3 full storeys.

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row '(default)' overlaid with the frontage row: A background house with no named record and no register row: the brick family's hip over the sheet's printed storeys, every face closed, nothing read beyond the sheet. Two 3B houses on a party wall behind the stone strip the sheet runs along their Indiana front, read as one ground (the 1904 grid gives 1615 and 1617 one lot): one record until T-1946 parts them; the small frame pieces at their rear are not drafted. Robinson 1886 draws a brick house with a stone front here. The sheet prints 3B on both houses; the trace reads 1617 as a range of 1615's body, so 'rear3B' holds it at the pair's full storeys. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 4197086797 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
